examples.en: The mother spoon-feeds porridge to the baby.
I spoon-fed soup to my sick friend.

examples.ko: 아이한테 밥을 떠먹이느라 제가 못 먹었어요.
examples.en: I was busy feeding my child with a spoon, so I couldn't eat.
I slowly fed rice gruel to Grandmother with a spoon.
I'm in the middle of spoon-feeding baby food to the baby.

examples.ko: 혼자 먹을 수 있는데 자꾸 떠먹이게 돼요.
examples.en: He can eat by himself, but I keep ending up spoon-feeding him.

explain: 숟가락으로 음식을 떠서 다른 사람 입에 넣어 주는 거예요. 그냥 '먹여 주다'보다 숟가락으로 떠서 준다는 모습이 분명해요. 아기, 환자, 어르신에게 많이 쓰고, '떠먹다'는 스스로 떠서 먹는 것이에요.

phrases.example: 모든 걸 떠먹여 줘야 하니까 힘들어요.
phrases.en: It's tiring because I have to spoon-feed him everything.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 하지 않아도 되게 모든 걸 다 해 주는 것을 뜻해요. 부정적으로 말할 때가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means doing everything for someone so they need not do anything themselves, often said negatively.

explain_en: It means scooping food with a spoon and putting it in another person's mouth. Compared with plain '먹여 주다', the image of using a spoon is clear. It is often used for babies, patients and elders, while '떠먹다' means scooping and eating by yourself.

examples.en: I boil soybean paste stew in an earthenware pot.

examples.ko: 뚝배기는 천천히 식어서 음식이 오래 따뜻해요.
examples.en: The earthenware pot cools slowly, so the food stays warm for a long time.
A sizzling hot pot came out at the restaurant.
My friend gave me a new earthenware pot as a gift.
Can I put the pot straight on the fire?

examples.ko: 추운 날에는 뚝배기 국밥이 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: On cold days I want to eat rice soup in a hot pot.

explain: 뚝배기는 찌개나 국을 끓여서 그대로 상에 올리는 그릇이에요. 쇠 냄비보다 천천히 끓고 천천히 식어서 상에 나온 뒤에도 보글보글해요. '뚝배기보다 장맛'이라는 속담은 겉보다 속이 중요할 때 써요.

phrases.en: I had bulgogi in an earthenware pot for lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뚝배기에 끓여서 나오는 불고기예요. 음식 이름으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Bulgogi served bubbling in a ttukbaegi. A common menu name.

phrases.en: I put the soup in a ttukbaegi and served it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 이 그릇에 넣을 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when putting food into this bowl.

phrases.en: As they say, taste matters more than the pot, and it's truly delicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습보다 속이 중요하다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning what's inside matters more than appearance.

explain_en: A 뚝배기 is a pot you boil stew or soup in and bring straight to the table. It heats and cools more slowly than a metal pot, so the food keeps bubbling at the table. The proverb '뚝배기보다 장맛' means the inside matters more than the looks.

examples.en: I spread margarine on my bread and ate it.
There was no butter, so I fried it with margarine.
Please keep the margarine in the fridge.
The margarine melted and spread across the pan.
Put one spoonful of margarine in the frying pan.
I bought margarine and flour at the mart.

explain: 버터와 비슷하게 빵에 바르거나 요리에 쓰지만 대개 식물성 기름으로 만들어요. 그래서 '버터' 대신 쓸 수 있는 재료로 이야기해요. 보통 '마가린을 바르다', '마가린을 두르다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I spread margarine on the bread and toasted it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빵에 얇게 펴 바를 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for spreading it thinly on bread.

phrases.en: I coated the pan with margarine and fried an egg.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 팬에 기름처럼 둘러 쓸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when coating a pan with it like oil while cooking.
phrases.en_equiv: to coat the pan with margarine

phrases.en: You can use margarine instead of butter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하게 쓰는 재료인 버터와 비교해 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when comparing it with butter, a similar ingredient.

explain_en: It is used like butter, for spreading on bread or cooking, but it is generally made from vegetable oil. So people talk about it as something to use instead of '버터'. It is usually said as '마가린을 바르다' or '마가린을 두르다'.

examples.en: In early summer, we pick plums and make plum syrup.

examples.ko: 할머니가 담근 매실차를 마셨더니 속이 편해졌어요.
examples.en: After drinking the plum tea Grandma made, my stomach felt better.
Plums are sour and hard to eat just like that.
I bought a box of plums at the mart.
I ate pickled plums with rice.
When plums ripen, they turn yellow.

explain: 한국의 '매실'은 서양 자두(plum)와 달라서 생으로 먹기보다 설탕에 절여 '매실청'으로 만들어요. 소화가 안 될 때 물에 타 마시는 가정이 많아요. 과일 '자두'와는 다른 과일이에요.

phrases.en: My grandmother makes plum syrup every year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매실을 설탕에 절인 것으로, 물에 타 마시거나 요리에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Plum preserved in sugar, mixed into water or used in cooking.

phrases.en: My stomach felt bad, so I drank plum tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매실청을 물에 타서 만든 차예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Tea made by mixing plum syrup with water.

phrases.en: There is one plum tree in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매실이 열리는 나무를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The tree that bears plums.

explain_en: Korean 매실 is not the same as the juicy Western plum; it is usually steeped in sugar to make 매실청 rather than eaten raw. Many households dilute it in water for an upset stomach. It is a different fruit from 자두.

examples.ko: 갓 구운 빵이 정말 먹음직해 보여요.
examples.en: The freshly baked bread looks really tempting.

examples.ko: 먹음직스러운 육회 위에 노른자가 동그랗게 얹혀 있었어요.
examples.en: A round egg yolk sat on top of the appetizing-looking raw beef.

examples.ko: 가게 앞에 먹음직한 과일이 가득 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: Delicious-looking fruit is piled up in front of the shop.

examples.ko: 사진 속 떡볶이가 너무 먹음직해서 배가 고파졌어요.
examples.en: The tteokbokki in the photo looked so good that I got hungry.
The meat is cooked so nicely, so please eat quickly.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 음식이 먹음직스럽게 나와서 사진 찍기 좋아요.
examples.en: This restaurant serves food that looks so appetizing that it's great for photos.

explain: '맛있다'는 먹어 보고 하는 말이고, '먹음직하다'는 보기만 해도 먹고 싶을 때 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '먹음직스럽다'도 많이 쓰는데, 이 말은 ㅂ 불규칙이라 '먹음직스러워요'가 돼요. '먹음직해 보이다'처럼 '보이다'와 자주 함께 써요.

phrases.en: The fruit on the plate looks delicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: '먹음직하다'와 같은 뜻이고 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '먹음직하다' and used more often.

phrases.en: This cake looks really tasty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보이다'와 함께 써서 겉모습을 보고 느낀 점을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '보이다' to describe an impression from appearance.

phrases.en: The shop is full of appetizing-looking bread.
phrases.nuance_ko: '먹음직한'이 음식 이름 앞에서 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: '먹음직한' goes before a food name to describe it.

explain_en: '맛있다' is what you say after eating, while '먹음직하다' is for food that makes you want to eat just by looking at it. '먹음직스럽다' means the same and is also common, but it is a ㅂ-irregular verb, so it becomes '먹음직스러워요'. It often goes with '보이다', as in '먹음직해 보이다'.

examples.en: The scent of quince fills the room.
My grandmother made me quince tea.

examples.ko: 모과는 단단하고 시어서 그냥 먹기 어려워요.
examples.en: Quince is hard and sour, so it is difficult to eat as it is.
When autumn came, the quinces ripened to yellow.

examples.ko: 차 안에 모과를 두면 향이 좋아요.
examples.en: If you leave a quince in the car, it smells nice.

examples.ko: 감기에 걸렸을 때 모과청을 타서 마셔요.
examples.en: When I have a cold, I mix quince syrup into water and drink it.

explain: 모과는 단단하고 시어서 그냥 먹기보다 차나 청으로 만들어 먹는 경우가 많아요. 그래서 '모과차', '모과청'이라는 말로 더 자주 들어요. 향이 좋아서 방이나 차 안에 두기도 해요.

phrases.en: I had a cold, so I drank warm quince tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모과를 먹는 가장 흔한 방법이라 표제어보다 더 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to eat quince, so you hear it more than the base word.

phrases.en: I pour hot water over quince preserve and drink it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모과를 설탕에 절인 것으로, 차를 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Quince preserved in sugar, used to make tea.

phrases.example: 차 안에 모과 향이 은은하게 나요.
phrases.en: A gentle scent of quince fills the car.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모과를 먹지 않고 향기를 즐길 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when enjoying the scent of quince rather than eating it.

explain_en: Quince is hard and sour, so people usually make it into tea or syrup rather than eating it plain. That is why you hear it more often in '모과차' and '모과청'. It smells nice, so some people keep one in a room or in the car.

examples.en: Steam is rising from the ramyeon.

examples.ko: 갓 쪄 낸 만두에서 김이 모락모락 올라와요.
examples.en: Steam is rising from the freshly steamed dumplings.

examples.ko: 국에서 모락모락 피어오르는 김을 보니 배가 고파져요.
examples.en: Seeing the steam curling up from the soup makes me hungry.

examples.ko: 모락모락 김이 나는 고구마를 호호 불어 먹었어요.
examples.en: I blew on the steaming sweet potato and ate it.

examples.ko: 겨울 아침에 따뜻한 밥에서 모락모락 김이 나요.
examples.en: On winter mornings, steam rises from the warm rice.

examples.ko: 추운 날에는 입에서도 입김이 모락모락 나요.
examples.en: On cold days, breath comes out of your mouth in puffs too.

explain: 김이나 연기가 천천히 계속 피어오르는 모양이에요. 따뜻한 음식에 쓰는 경우가 많아서 '김이 모락모락 나다'로 가장 자주 써요. '펄펄'처럼 세게 끓는 느낌과 달리 조용히 올라와요.

phrases.example: 김이 모락모락 나는 국을 호호 불어서 먹어요.
phrases.en: I blow on the steaming soup and eat it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나는'을 붙여 뜨거운 음식을 꾸며 주는 말로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 나는, it describes a hot food that is giving off steam.

phrases.en: Smoke is rising in wisps from the chimney.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식뿐 아니라 굴뚝이나 모닥불의 연기에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works not only for food but also for smoke from chimneys or campfires.

phrases.example: 갓 삶은 감자에서 김이 모락모락 올라요.
phrases.en: Steam is rising from the freshly boiled potatoes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나다' 대신 '오르다'를 쓰면 김이 위로 올라가는 모습이 더 잘 느껴져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using 오르다 instead of 나다 makes the upward movement of the steam clearer.

explain_en: It describes steam or smoke rising slowly and steadily. It is mostly used for warm food, so '김이 모락모락 나다' is the most common form. Unlike '펄펄', which feels like hard boiling, it rises quietly.

en: to mix; to season; to stir

examples.en: I blanch spinach and toss it with sesame oil.
My mother is seasoning bean sprouts.

examples.ko: 나물을 무칠 때는 양념을 조금씩 넣어요.
examples.en: When I season vegetables, I add the seasoning little by little.
I salted the cucumber and then mixed it with chili powder.

examples.ko: 간장과 참기름에 무치면 간단한 반찬이 돼요.
examples.en: Tossed in soy sauce and sesame oil, it becomes an easy side dish.

examples.ko: 손으로 살살 무쳐야 나물이 부서지지 않아요.
examples.en: You need to toss it gently by hand so the greens don't break.

explain: 나물이나 채소에 양념을 넣고 섞는 요리를 말해요. 김치처럼 속을 가득 버무릴 때는 '버무리다'를 많이 쓰고, 밥에 섞을 때는 '비비다'를 써요. 소리가 비슷한 '사무치다'는 전혀 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: I seasoned some namul over the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나물'과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with 무치다.

phrases.en: I mix cucumbers with soy sauce and eat them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무쳐서 바로 먹는다는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connected form meaning you season it and eat it.

phrases.en: Mom seasoned the spinach deliciously for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남을 위해 해 줄 때는 '-아/어 주다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -아/어 주다 when doing it for someone else.

explain_en: It's for mixing seasoning into vegetables or greens. For coating something thoroughly like kimchi filling, '버무리다' is common, and for mixing with rice you use '비비다'. The similar-sounding '사무치다' is a completely different word.

t90.ax: My mother is seasoning bean sprouts.

examples.en: The seasoned bellflower root suits my taste perfectly.

examples.ko: 식당에서 나물 무침을 한 접시 더 시켰어요.
examples.en: I ordered one more plate of seasoned greens at the restaurant.

examples.ko: 무침은 양념이 중요해서 간을 잘 봐야 해요.
examples.en: For seasoned dishes the seasoning matters, so you need to taste it well.

examples.ko: 어머니의 무침 맛은 아무도 못 따라가요.
examples.en: No one can match the taste of my mother's seasoned dishes.
I added a little vinegar to this seasoned dish.

examples.ko: 밥이랑 무침만 있어도 한 끼가 충분해요.
examples.en: Rice and a seasoned side dish alone make a good meal.

explain: 보통 '오이무침', '콩나물무침'처럼 재료 이름 뒤에 붙여 써요. 주로 반찬이고, 같은 재료로 만든 '볶음'이나 '조림'과는 만드는 방법이 달라요.

phrases.en: Today's side dish is seasoned cucumber.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료 이름에 붙여 한 단어처럼 쓰는 가장 흔한 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pattern, attached to an ingredient like one word.

phrases.en: Seasoned side dishes are sweet and sour and bring back my appetite.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반찬 종류를 말할 때 '볶음 반찬', '조림 반찬'과 나란히 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used alongside 볶음 반찬 and 조림 반찬 to name types of side dishes.

phrases.en: I made seasoned spinach over the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 직접 만든다고 할 때 '만들다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 만들다 when saying you made the dish.

explain_en: It's usually attached to an ingredient, as in '오이무침' or '콩나물무침'. It's mostly a side dish, and it is made differently from '볶음' (stir-fried) or '조림' (braised) dishes with the same ingredient.

examples.en: Please simmer it gently until the broth gets rich.

examples.ko: 약한 불에서 뭉근히 졸이면 맛이 깊어져요.
examples.en: If you reduce it slowly over low heat, the flavor gets deeper.
I boiled the meat slowly, and it's very tender.
Red bean porridge tastes good when you stir it slowly for a long time.

examples.ko: 찌개가 뭉근히 끓는 동안 밥을 지었어요.
examples.en: I cooked rice while the stew simmered gently.
I slow-simmered ox bones to make seolleongtang.

explain: 센 불이 아니라 약한 불에서 오래 천천히 조리할 때 써요. '끓이다, 졸이다, 고다, 삶다'와 잘 어울리고 요리법 글에서 자주 나와요. '푹'은 충분히 오래 익힌다는 느낌이라 불 세기와는 상관없어요.

phrases.en: I simmered the beef bones slowly to make the broth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약한 불에서 오래 끓이는 방법을 말할 때 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for slow simmering.

phrases.en: Braised dishes need slow reducing to absorb flavor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양념이 스며들게 천천히 줄일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when slowly reducing a sauce so flavors soak in.

phrases.en: Stir the porridge over low heat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뭉근하다'의 활용형으로 약한 불을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form of 뭉근하다, describing low heat.

explain_en: It is used when cooking slowly over low heat rather than high heat. It pairs well with '끓이다', '졸이다', '고다' and '삶다', and often appears in recipes. '푹' means cooking thoroughly for a long time and says nothing about the heat level.

examples.en: I ordered clam noodle soup.
You have to let clams purge, so the sand comes out.
I bought fresh clams at the market.
Adding clams to soybean stew makes it refreshing.

examples.ko: 바지락이 입을 벌리면 다 익은 거예요.
examples.en: When the clams open their shells, they're done.
I dug up clams at the beach.

explain: 조개 중에서도 칼국수나 된장찌개 같은 국물 요리에 가장 흔하게 들어가요. 요리 전에 소금물에 담가 모래를 빼는 일을 '해감'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 속이 안 좋을 때 바지락탕을 먹어요.
phrases.en: When my stomach feels bad, I eat clam soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바지락을 넣고 끓인 맑은 국물 요리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A clear soup boiled with short-necked clams.

phrases.en: You have to purge the clams of sand before cooking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모래를 빼려고 소금물에 담그는 요리 전 준비 과정을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The prep step of soaking clams in salt water to remove sand.

phrases.en: Tonight's dinner is soybean paste stew with clams.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바지락이 들어간 된장찌개로, 국물이 시원해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Soybean paste stew with clams, known for its refreshing broth.

explain_en: It is the clam most commonly put into broths such as 칼국수 and 된장찌개. Soaking clams in salt water to remove sand before cooking is called 해감.

examples.en: The cherries on the cherry tree have ripened to black.

examples.ko: 봄이 지나면 길에 버찌가 많이 떨어져요.
examples.en: After spring passes, many cherries fall on the street.
If you step on cherries, your shoes get stained dark red.
The children picked cherries and put them in their mouths.
Cherry-blossom-tree cherries are much smaller than regular cherries.

examples.ko: 이 버찌로 잼을 만들 수 있을까요?
examples.en: Can we make jam with these cherries?

explain: 벚나무의 열매예요. 체리와 비슷하게 생겼지만, 먹으려고 사는 과일은 보통 '체리'라고 해요. 길가의 벚나무 아래에서 봄이 끝날 무렵에 많이 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The fruit of the cherry tree has ripened to black.
phrases.nuance_ko: '버찌'를 풀어서 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spelled-out way of saying 버찌.

phrases.en: The children picked up and collected cherries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 떨어진 버찌를 줍는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes picking up fallen cherries.

phrases.example: 버찌를 밟았더니 신발에 버찌 물이 들었어요.
phrases.en: I stepped on cherries and my shoes got stained.
phrases.nuance_ko: 버찌가 터져서 묻은 검붉은 색을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the dark red stain left by squashed cherries.

explain_en: This is the fruit of the cherry-blossom tree. It looks like a cherry, but the fruit people buy to eat is usually called '체리'. You can often see them under roadside cherry trees around the end of spring.

t90.ax: Can we make jam with these cherries?

examples.ko: 속이 안 좋을 때는 북엇국이 최고예요.
examples.en: When your stomach feels bad, bugeoguk is the best.
I beat an egg and stirred it into the dried pollack soup.
I ordered the dried pollack soup set meal at the restaurant.
For breakfast I had warm dried pollack soup and rice.
Bugeoguk is popular because the broth is refreshing.
The bugeoguk my mom makes is the tastiest.

explain: 북어를 넣고 끓인 맑고 시원한 국이에요. 속이 불편할 때 찾는 사람이 많아요. 달걀을 풀거나 두부, 무를 넣어서 끓이는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I cooked dried pollack soup this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국을 만들 때는 '끓이다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 끓이다 for cooking a soup.

phrases.en: A bowl of dried pollack soup settles my stomach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국은 '그릇'으로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Soup is counted with the counter 그릇.
phrases.en_equiv: a bowl of dried pollack soup

phrases.en: This restaurant's dried pollack soup is really refreshing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국어에서 맑고 개운한 국물 맛을 '시원하다'고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In Korean, a clean, refreshing broth taste is called 시원하다.

explain_en: It is a clear, refreshing soup made with dried pollack. Many people reach for it when their stomach feels uneasy. It is often cooked with beaten egg, tofu or radish.

examples.en: I bought a bag of puffed grain snack at the market.
I left the bag open, and the puffed snack got soggy.

examples.ko: 뻥튀기 기계에서 '뻥!' 소리가 나서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The puffing machine went 'bang!' and I was startled.
Puffed grain snacks are light and nutty, so they make a good snack.
Instead of cookies, a puffed grain snack is a good snack too.
I had a puffed grain snack together with warm tea.

explain: 쌀이나 옥수수 같은 곡식을 기계에 넣어 '뻥' 하고 부풀려 만든 과자예요. '뻥'이 거짓말이나 과장을 뜻하는 말이어서, 비유로 숫자나 이야기를 부풀릴 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I heard the company announced inflated sales figures.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자나 이야기를 실제보다 크게 부풀린다는 뜻으로 구어에서 써요. 조금 속된 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in casual speech for blowing numbers or stories up bigger than they really are. It sounds a bit slangy.

explain_en: It is a snack made by putting grains like rice or corn in a machine that puffs them with a 'bang'. Because '뻥' is also slang for a lie or exaggeration, it is used figuratively for inflating numbers or stories.

examples.en: The farmers are having their mid-work snack in the rice field.
Before lunch, we ate noodles as a snack.

examples.ko: 새참 시간이 되면 일을 잠깐 멈춰요.
examples.en: When it's snack time, we pause work for a moment.

examples.ko: 일하는 중에 새참이 오니까 힘이 났어요.
examples.en: The snack arrived while we were working, so I got energized.
A snack break meal is usually something simple.

examples.ko: 새참도 챙겨 가야 하니까 짐이 많아요.
examples.en: I have to bring the snacks too, so I have a lot to carry.

explain: 농사일이나 공사처럼 오래 일하는 중간에 먹는 간단한 음식과 그 시간을 말해요. 평범한 '간식'과 달리 일하는 사이에 먹는다는 느낌이 있어서 시골 풍경을 떠올리게 해요. '참'이라고 줄여서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I ate a snack under a tree while working.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하는 중간에 간단히 먹을 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for eating a quick bite mid-work.

phrases.en: It's snack time, so we're taking a short break.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하는 중간의 쉬는 시간을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the break time in the middle of work.

phrases.en: We had a snack in the middle of work and started again.
phrases.nuance_ko: '새참'을 줄인 말로, 시골에서 많이 들을 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of '새참', often heard in the countryside.

explain_en: It means the light food, and the time for it, in the middle of long work such as farming or construction. Unlike a plain '간식', it carries the sense of eating between work, so it evokes the countryside. People also shorten it to '참'.

t90.ax: Before lunch, we ate noodles as a snack.
